record.context_brief: Representing algebraic lattices by weak congruence lattices
record.original_question: Given an algebraic lattice L and a chosen element a of L, determine the conditions under which there exists an algebra whose weak congruence lattice is isomorphic to L and whose diagonal equality relation corresponds to a under the isomorphism. The source notes that all weak congruences form an algebraic lattice under inclusion, that the diagonal relation has a particular role, and that not every element can occur because the chosen element should be codistributive and satisfy additional conditions.

evidence.quote: All weak congruences form an algebraic lattice under inclusion.
The diagonal relation (equality) has a particular role within weak congruence lattice.
under which conditions there is an algebra such that its weak congruence lattice is isomorphic to L and the diagonal element corresponds to the fixed element a under this isomorphism.
This is not possible for every element in a lattice, since this element should be codistributive and should satisfy some particular conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{A} = (A, F)$ be an algebra. A binary relation $\rho \subseteq A \times A$ is called a weak congruence on $\mathbb{A}$ if it is symmetric, transitive, and compatible with all operations in $F$ (note: reflexivity is not required, so $\rho$ is a congruence on some subalgebra of $\mathbb{A}$). The set $\mathrm{Cw}(\mathbb{A})$ of all weak congruences on $\mathbb{A}$, ordered by inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice; the diagonal $\Delta_A = \{(x,x) : x \in A\}$ is a distinguished element of this lattice.

An element $u$ of an algebraic lattice $L$ is called codistributive if $u \vee (x \wedge y) = (u \vee x) \wedge (u \vee y)$ for all $x, y \in L$.

Problem. Let $L$ be an algebraic lattice and let $a \in L$ be a fixed element. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(L, a)$ under which there exists an algebra $\mathbb{A}$ together with a lattice isomorphism $\varphi : L \to \mathrm{Cw}(\mathbb{A})$ such that $\varphi(a) = \Delta_A$.

(It is known that any such element $a$ must be codistributive in $L$, and must satisfy further restrictions, so the problem asks for a complete characterization of the "diagonal-suitable" pairs $(L, a)$.)
artifact.status_search_result: The representation problem for algebraic lattices as weak congruence lattices of algebras, with a designated diagonal element, is a known long-standing open problem in universal algebra. Partial results exist (necessary codistributivity, atomistic case, fuzzy-valued variants, characterization for groups), but a complete characterization of "Δ-suitable" pairs (L, a) has not been established.

status_evidence.title: A note on atomistic weak congruence lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Codistributive elements and applications to weak congruence lattices; partial results in atomistic case.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results on the Δ-suitability problem are known.

status_evidence.title: A note on representation of lattices by weak congruences
status_evidence.snippet: Representation of lattices by weak congruences remains a topic of active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The general representation problem is still under study.

status_evidence.title: Representation of lattices by fuzzy weak congruence relations
status_evidence.snippet: A wider class of lattices can be represented in the fuzzy framework than in the classical one.
status_evidence.claim: Classical representation by weak congruences is restrictive and incomplete.
